## Monday, 2026-09-28 | ERCOT BESS Fleet (32 Nodes)

---

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet average RT settled at **$45.39/MWh**, a sharp acceleration from the prior 3-day trend ($36.37 → $37.84 → $32.31), representing a **+40% RT price surge** driven by late-summer heat load across the Texas interior. An extraordinary **28 of 32 nodes** breached the $100/MWh spike threshold — the broadest congestion event in the recent 5-day window — with fleet peak RT reaching **$201.53/MWh**. The congestion fingerprint is geographically diffuse, spanning West Texas (TOYAH, SADLBACK, FAULKNER), South Texas (CATARINA, FALFUR, TYNAN), and Panhandle/North corridors (OLNEYTN, DIBOL), suggesting systemic transmission stress rather than isolated locational events. **CATARINA_B1** was the standout congestion beneficiary at **+$154.94/MWh MCC**, while **FALFUR_RN** (-$27.90/MWh MCC) and **MV_VALV4_RN** (-$23.54/MWh MCC) absorbed material congestion costs despite strong DA premium capture. Notably, **TOYAH_RN** and four other bottom-DART nodes showed RT exceeding DA by modest margins ($0.02–$0.47/MWh), indicating those nodes captured **RT outperformance** if dispatched in real-time — not a strategic miss.

---

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

**Today (09-28):** Heat is the dominant theme across the entire ERCOT footprint — Laredo at 102°F, Brownsville 99°F, Austin/San Antonio 97°F, DFW 92°F, Midland 94°F. With virtually no precipitation risk today (<22% everywhere), expect gross load to remain elevated above yesterday's 81.6 GW print, sustaining RT price pressure particularly in HE14–HE16 (peak cooling demand) and HE21–HE23 (retained heat, slow load release). The current conditions are highly favorable for a repeat of yesterday's widespread spike environment — **BESS operators should target full charge by HE11 and prioritize discharge at HE14–HE16 and HE22–HE23.**

**09-29 through 10-01 — The Transition:** A significant weather system moves through beginning Tuesday, with Lubbock (65% precip), Victoria (64%), Wichita Falls (83% by 09-30), and near-certain precipitation across San Antonio (99%), Austin (95%), DFW (100%), and Laredo (98%) by 10-01. This represents a **major demand destruction event** — temperatures drop 10–20°F across the interior by 10-01, and solar generation will likely be curtailed by cloud cover. Expect RT prices to compress materially Thursday-Friday, reducing spread opportunity. **DA offers for 09-30 and 10-01 should be sized conservatively** — DA premiums may increase as RT softens, but load-weighted average prices will likely fall toward the $25–$35/MWh range.

**10-02 through 10-04 — Post-Frontal Uncertainty:** Residual moisture lingers across the Coast (Brownsville/Corpus 75–83% precip), but interior Texas begins drying. Temperatures stabilize in the mid-70s to low-80s — **load drops into fall range, eliminating the heat-premium that has characterized this week**. Wind generation may increase post-frontal, adding renewable pressure on prices. This window likely represents the lowest RT pricing environment of the 7-day outlook; consider positioning for **ancillary service revenue capture** (NSPIN/ECRS) rather than energy arbitrage as energy margins compress.

HEN's custom index performance reveals a **significant structural advantage** from the fleet's RT-heavy revenue profile: **HEN 2026 at $20,757/MW/yr** outperforms the 1-Hr Without HEN benchmark ($15,873/MW/yr) by **$4,884/MW/yr (+31%)**, driven almost entirely by HEN's energy_rtm revenue stream ($11,139/MW/yr vs. the market benchmark's $2,719/MW/yr). This confirms that HEN's real-time dispatch strategy has been the primary alpha generator year-to-date, not DA energy commitment — an important context for interpreting yesterday's RT spike performance. The **Fort Duncan** 2-hr index at **$35,952/MW/yr** outperforms its 2-hr market peers ($30,421/MW/yr) by +$5,531/MW/yr, led by an extraordinary energy_rtm contribution of **$24,265/MW/yr** (vs. $11,776/MW/yr for non-HEN 2-hr peers) — Fort Duncan's RT energy dominance validates the Lean DA recommendation and suggests continued RT optionality should be preserved at FTDUNCAN_RN. Note these indices run through 2026-07-28 (210/190 days), so the September heat spike is not yet captured — the YTD outperformance gap likely widens materially when August–September settlements are incorporated.

## 6. AS MARKET ANALYSIS (3-Day Trailing: 09-25 through 09-27)

**NSPIN is the most compelling DA offer opportunity** for 2026-09-28, with a 3-day average DA-RT spread of **+$2.72/MW** — the highest of any service — and a sharply accelerating daily trend ($1.37 → $2.92 → $3.87), culminating in a **peak HE21 spread of +$30.27/MW on 09-27** and an HE22 average (3-day) of +$16.05/MW. REGUP and RRS show consistent but more modest 3-day premiums (+$0.73/MW each), with HE21–HE23 as the peak spread window for both — the convergence of NSPIN, ECRS, REGUP, and RRS all peaking in the **HE21–HE23 window confirms that AS DA offers stacked in the evening block represent today's highest-confidence ancillary revenue opportunity.** One DA offer risk flag: **REGDN at HE18 showed -$4.43/MW on 09-27** (RT exceeded DA), and NSPIN at HE24 printed -$5.37/MW on the same day — avoid REGDN and NSPIN DA offers in the late-overnight hours where RT has repeatedly outrun DA commitments.
